label: PER_SE_5, per se actual cause of being: an actual cause of x's esse that causes it as caused
term: per se actual cause of being (PerSeActualEsseCause)
definition: PerSeActualEsseCause p AsCaused c x: c is an actual cause of the esse of x (ActualEsseCause: c other than x, both in act as to being, CausesIn c x esse, mode of causing unspecified, tenseless) and AsCaused c x. AsCaused is a primitive per se link: c causes the esse of x only insofar as c's own esse is caused, so that c's being caused is not accidental to its causing x's esse. It is modelled on ST I q.46 a.2 ad 7, which speaks of efficient causes: there, causes 'quae per se requiruntur ad aliquem effectum' (stone, stick, hand; a man's generation depending on the elementary body and the sun) form a per se series, while successive hammers, or generators who all 'habent gradum unum in causis efficientibus' and of whom it is accidental 'inquantum generat, quod sit generatus ab alio', form a per accidens one. AsCaused is not defined from well-foundedness, time, simultaneity, efficiency or conservation, and no structural property (transitivity, asymmetry) is assumed; it is constrained only by the premises that use it. With AsCaused everywhere true or everywhere false the predicates using it become trivial, so their content is the intended meaning of this primitive.
note: Stipulated for #1635 as an analyst analogue, for causes of esse of unspecified mode, of the per se order that ad 7 (pinned passage a34be6a3, read) states for efficient causes; applying it to causes of esse is the analyst's. It would be sourced by a passage stating a per se order among causes of being. It is sense PER_SE_5 of DISAMB-PER-SE; its relation to PER_SE_1 (the prima via's per se ordered series, and the secunda via's CausesAsCaused for efficient causes) is open and not asserted. See docs/notes/de-ente-esse-source-1628.md, section on the per se regress.
